prompt: Which sentence is the contrapositive of p ⇒ q?
explanation: The contrapositive swaps and negates both sides, and it is equivalent to the original.

prompt: p is true and q is false. Which sentence is true?
explanation: An implication with a false antecedent is true, so q ⇒ p holds.

prompt: From the line p ∧ q, which rule gives you q in one step?
explanation: And Elimination takes a conjunction apart into its conjuncts.

prompt: The lines p and p ⇒ q are on the board. Which rule concludes q?
explanation: Implication Elimination (modus ponens) takes p and p ⇒ q to q.

prompt: Which sentence does p ∧ q logically entail?
explanation: Whenever p ∧ q is true, p is true, and so is any disjunction containing p.

prompt: Which sentence says "everything is p"?
explanation: ∀X.p(X) says p holds of every object.

prompt: From ∀X.p(X), what can Universal Elimination give you?
explanation: Universal Elimination substitutes a ground term for the variable.

prompt: Which sentence is equivalent to ¬(p ∧ q)?
explanation: De Morgan's law: a conjunction is false exactly when one of its conjuncts is.

prompt: Which sentence is true under every truth assignment?
explanation: If p is true, q ⇒ p is true; if p is false, the whole implication is true.

prompt: What is the usual way to prove p ⇒ q in Fitch?
choices: Assume q, derive p, then apply Implication Introduction
Prove p and q separately, then apply And Introduction
Assume p, derive q, then apply Implication Introduction
explanation: Implication Introduction discharges the assumption p once q is reached inside the subproof.

prompt: The premises are p ∨ q and ¬p. Which sentence follows?
explanation: One of p, q is true and it is not p, so it is q.

prompt: Or Elimination concludes r from p ∨ q and which two other lines?
explanation: If each disjunct leads to r, then r follows from the disjunction.

prompt: Which sentence is equivalent to ¬∀X.p(X)?
explanation: Not everything is p exactly when something is not p.

prompt: When may Universal Introduction generalize p(c) to ∀X.p(X)?
choices: When c appears in one of the premises
When p(c) is itself a premise
Whenever p(c) is on the board
When c is arbitrary: it appears in no premise and no open assumption
explanation: Only a name nothing has pinned down can stand for every object.

prompt: The language has exactly the object constants a and b, and no functions. Which lines let Domain Closure conclude ∀X.p(X)?
explanation: Domain Closure needs the instance for every object constant in the language.

prompt: Which set of premises entails r?
explanation: Each case of p ∨ q leads to r. The others each have an assignment where r is false.

prompt: In this Fitch system there is no rule for false. How is ¬p proved?
choices: Assume p, derive p, then apply Negation Elimination
Derive p ⇒ q and p ⇒ ¬q for some q, then apply Negation Introduction
Assume ¬p, derive ¬p, then apply Implication Introduction
explanation: Negation Introduction takes two implications from p to a sentence and its negation.

prompt: Which sentence is equivalent to p ⇔ q?
explanation: p ⇔ q holds when p and q agree: both true or both false.

prompt: Which sentence is valid?
explanation: One X related to every Y gives every Y some X. The converse fails: each Y may need a different X.

prompt: Existential Elimination takes ∃X.p(X) and ∀X.(p(X) ⇒ q) to q. Why does it refuse when the second line is ∀X.(p(X) ⇒ q(X)) instead?
choices: X would occur free in the conclusion
p(X) has to be a premise
Universal Elimination has to be applied first
explanation: The conclusion ψ may not mention the variable, or it would claim q of an unknown object.

prompt: Of the four truth assignments to p and q, how many make (p ⇒ q) ∧ (q ⇒ p) ∧ (p ∨ q) true?
explanation: The first two conjuncts make p and q agree; p ∨ q rules out both false. Only both true is left.

prompt: Prove p ⇒ r from p ⇒ q and q ⇒ r.
explanation: Assume p, use Implication Elimination twice to reach r, then discharge with Implication Introduction.

prompt: Prove p ∧ q ⇒ r from p ⇒ (q ⇒ r).
explanation: Assume p ∧ q, take it apart with And Elimination, then apply Implication Elimination twice.

prompt: Prove r ∧ (p ∨ q) from p ∨ q, p ⇒ r and q ⇒ r.
explanation: Or Elimination gives r from the disjunction and its two cases; And Introduction joins it to p ∨ q.

prompt: Prove ¬q ⇒ ¬p from p ⇒ q.
explanation: Assume ¬q. Inside, show p ⇒ ¬q by assuming p and reiterating ¬q; Negation Introduction with p ⇒ q gives ¬p.

prompt: Prove p ⇒ (q ⇒ r) from p ∧ q ⇒ r.
explanation: Assume p, then q, join them with And Introduction, fire the premise, and discharge both assumptions in turn.

prompt: Prove q ∨ p from p ∨ q.
explanation: Prove p ⇒ q ∨ p and q ⇒ q ∨ p with Or Introduction inside two subproofs, then use Or Elimination.
